paragraphs.text: PDF text extraction that survives CID/ObjStm fonts (CVPR/IEEE PDFs) — DSH/Cordis tools
# @rrdongdong/dsh-pdf

> **Not affiliated with DeepSeek.** "DeepSeek Harness (DSH)" and "Cordis" are used
> descriptively;
this is a community plugin, not an official package.

Two DSH (Cordis) tools for reading papers:
**`pdf_fetch`** — resumable, integrity-checked download;

**`pdf_extract`** — text extraction that
survives **subsetted CID fonts**, **ToUnicode CMaps**, and
**compressed object streams (`/ObjStm`)**.
中文说明见 README.zh.md.
## Why this exists
Most PDFs are fine. CVPR/CVF (and some IEEE) PDFs are not: their fonts are subsetted CID fonts, so a
glyph byte only means something after a `/ToUnicode` CMap lookup — and those font dictionaries are
themselves packed inside **compressed object streams**. A naive scraper therefore:
| Step | What a naive stream scraper does | Result |
| Look for font maps | `/ToUnicode` appears **0 times** in raw bytes (it lives inside `/ObjStm`) | n

o character mapping at all |
| Treat streams as text | 4 vector-figure streams of **12–14 MB** happe

n to contain `BT`/`Tj`-like tokens | ~50 MB of drawing commands parsed |
| Outcome | hangs, then emi
ts garbage | "the paper has no text" — except it does |

`pdfjs-dist` handles both. Measured on an 11.2 MB CVPR 2026 paper: **86 ms to load**, 10,525
charact
ers from the first 3 pages, 100 % printable.
### Measured before / after (same file)
| | naive scraper | this plugin |
| Download | 3 failures (timeout, truncated at 1.48 MB, SIGTERM) | **6.3 s, 1 attempt, 8.94 MB, `%%E

OF` verified** |
| Extraction | font maps = 0; 100 s hang; 682 KB of mojibake | **13 pages, clean te

xt** |
| On a truncated file | silent garbage | `PDF_TRUNCATED: 未找到 %%EOF 标记 …` |
## Requirements
**Node ≥ 22.13.** `pdfjs-dist@6` needs `Promise.withResolvers`; on an older runtime the plugin raise

s
a named `NODE_TOO_OLD` error instead of failing deep inside pdfjs. Consumers stuck on Node 20 can

pin
`pdfjs-dist@4.x` (same CID/ToUnicode support, older runtime floor).
## Install (DSH profile)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> Installing from npm instead (`npm i @rrdongdong/dsh-pdf`) works too, but the plugin must be
> reso

lvable from the **profile's** `node_modules` — a symlink into
> `~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/@r
rdongdong/` is the least invasive way.
### Never restart blind
`ToolRuntime.register()` rejects a definition whose `output` lacks `render`, and that throw happens

**while the plugin tree loads** — so the whole gateway fails to boot, not just this plugin.
`defineT
ool()` does not validate it, so the mistake stays invisible until the host is already down.
`bin/preflight.mjs` mirrors the registration-time checks **before** you touch a running host:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Step **[5]** is the important one. When the host's `dsh-tools` cannot be resolved, the plugin
compil

es schemas itself; a fallback that is *stricter or looser* than the host silently changes
behaviour,

so preflight asserts byte-for-byte equality with `defineTool()` whenever the host copy is
available

. (Writing this check immediately caught a real divergence: the host treats a parameter root
as an i
mplicit **open** object, while the first fallback emitted `additionalProperties: false`.)
## Tools
### `pdf_extract(path, pages?, maxChars?)`
| parameter | |

| `path` *(required)* | absolute, or relative to the process cwd |
| `pages` | `"1-5"`, `"3"`, `"1,4

-6"`, or `"all"` (default) |
| `maxChars` | default `200000`; sets `truncated: true` when hit |
| re
turns | `{ pageCount, pagesExtracted[], chars, truncated, text }` |

Read-only. Fails fast with stable codes: `PDF_NOT_FOUND`, `PDF_NOT_A_FILE`, `PDF_TOO_SMALL`,
`PDF_TO
O_LARGE`, `PDF_BAD_MAGIC`, `PDF_TRUNCATED`, `PDF_BAD_PAGES`.
### `pdf_fetch(url, force?, attempts?, perAttemptTimeoutMs?)`

Downloads into a **private cache under the OS temp root** with `Range` resume, retries, and a
`%%EOF
` check. Returns `{ path, bytes, attempts, complete, cached, error? }`.

`complete: false` means **do not parse it**. A half-downloaded PDF is worse than a missing one: it
p
arses into plausible-looking garbage instead of failing.
## Config

Every key optional; validated eagerly, so a typo fails at the plugin row rather than mid-download.
U
nknown keys are rejected.
| key | default | meaning |

| `cacheDir` | `os.tmpdir()/dsh-pdf-cache` | where `pdf_fetch` writes (resolved to absolute) |
| `ma

xPdfBytes` | `268435456` (256 MiB) | refuse to read larger files |
| `defaultMaxChars` | `200000` |

text cap when the caller omits `maxChars` |
| `fetchAttempts` | `4` | total attempts (each resumes f

rom the byte offset) |
| `fetchPerAttemptTimeoutMs` | `90000` | per-attempt timeout |
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Design constraints (each learned by breaking something)
1. **Never depend on `@deepseek-ai/*` from a public registry.** Mirrors may carry an older version,

and a second copy of `dsh-tools` means a duplicate service instance that breaks tool
registration. T

his plugin resolves the host's own copy and falls back to a local, parity-tested
compiler.
2. **A pl

ugin must not write user files with `node:fs`.** That bypasses the host's filesystem policy.
Downloa

ds go to a private temp cache only; extraction is read-only.
3. **Truncation must fail loudly.** Sil

ent garbage poisons every downstream consumer.
4. **`output.render` is mandatory** — and its absence
is discovered only at boot, hence preflight.
## Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]
CI runs both on **Node 22 and 24** with a small checked-in fixture. `bin/preflight.mjs` degrades to

offline checks when no DSH runtime is present (that is the CI case): host-dependent stages are
skipp

en no DSH runtime is present (that is the CI case): host-dependent stages are
skipped, never failed.
## License
MIT — see LICENSE.

Third-party components are **not** vendored: the only runtime dependency is
`pdfjs-dist` (**Apache-2

.0**), installed by npm and subject to its
own license. Our `bin/preflight.mjs` intentionally *mirro

rs* the registration-time validation of
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (MIT) so that a plugin author can c

atch a host-fatal definition problem before
restarting a host; it is an independent implementation,

not copied code. See
`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`.
